citation: Alexander Lowen, The Way to Vibrant Health
name: Jaw, sound, neck, settle
summary: Seven and a half minutes on the throat, jaw and voice: pull faces, stretch and massage the neck, then lie down and hold a long open 'ahhh' until the voice does whatever it does. Reach for it on a morning when the check-in sounds clipped, articulate and a little cut off — when he is explaining his state rather than feeling it, when the jaw is set, or when he says he wants to cry and can't get there. Skip it freely; it is meant to be irregular, and a morning it gets skipped on purpose is a good morning.

steps.title: 1. Ground and sound
steps.text: Stand with your feet parallel about eight inches apart, knees soft, weight forward on the balls of your feet, belly out, pelvis loose and tipped back. Take four or five deep audible belly breaths through an open mouth and let a sound ride out on each one. (Ex. 13)

steps.title: 2. Jaw and face
steps.text: Stick the jaw out, show your teeth, make an angry face and let sound come with it. Then move the jaw up and down strongly, then left and right as far as it goes, and finish with the jaw back and soft, mouth open, reaching your lips out the way a baby does. Trembling in the jaw or tingling around the mouth is the exercise working. (Ex. 62)

steps.title: 3. Neck
steps.text: Sit cross-legged, lace your fingers behind your head and pull it slowly down, letting the head fully yield, then bend forward so the stretch runs on down your back. Come back up and use your thumbs to massage the tight bands alongside the spine, from the root of the neck to the base of the skull. (Ex. 60)

steps.title: 4. Voice
steps.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, head tipped back to open the throat. Make a moderately loud 'ahhh' and hold it as long as it goes without forcing, then take an easy breath and start again. Don't push the sound — forcing only tightens the throat. If the voice starts to tremble or turns into a sob, let it. (Ex. 5-B)

steps.title: 5. Fold and settle
steps.text: Stand and hang forward, knees slightly bent, fingertips toward the floor, and let the legs shake out whatever built up. Then sit, soften your eyes, and take a few long exhales. (Ex. 1)

citation: Alexander Lowen, The Way to Vibrant Health
name: Shoulders, reach, arch, settle
summary: Seven minutes working the shoulder girdle before the spine: shrugs and rolls, a loud elbow thrust, reaching forward from the shoulders rather than the hands, then arching back over a bolster placed high, at the tips of the shoulder blades. Reach for it when the morning report is a slouch, a rounded upper back, shoulders up around the ears, or a whole week spent hunched at a desk — this is the mechanical fix for the posture, done by releasing rather than by sitting up straight. Needs a bolster or rolled blanket, and is meant to be taken up irregularly rather than daily.

steps.title: 1. Shrug and roll
steps.text: Stand in the basic position — feet parallel, knees soft, weight forward, belly out. Lift the shoulders slowly and let them drop as if shrugging off the whole day, then roll them up, forward, down and back several times, and reverse. Breathe in as they rise, out as they fall. (Ex. 42, 58a)

steps.title: 2. Get off my back
steps.text: Bend your elbows and raise them to shoulder height, then thrust both elbows back hard and say 'get off my back' out loud. Repeat a handful of times and feel your back straighten. Keep it short and postural — this is a stretch that happens to have a voice, not an anger session. (Ex. 43)

steps.title: 3. Reach from the heart
steps.text: Reach forward with hands and arms, then extend the reach further by letting the shoulders come forward as you breathe out; draw them back as you breathe in, and reach again. Then stretch the arms out to the sides and flap them, leaning forward, faster and faster as if you could take off. (Ex. 58c, 41)

steps.title: 4. Arch over the roll
steps.text: Lie back over a bolster or rolled blanket placed high — at the lower tips of the shoulder blades, roughly the nipple line, above where you usually put it. Knees bent, feet flat, arms reaching back over your head toward a chair or the floor. Sound on every exhale. Two minutes at the outside, then come up. (Ex. 83)

steps.title: 5. Fold and settle
steps.text: Come off the roll and rest for a few breaths with your hands behind your head before you get up. Then stand and hang forward, knees soft, and let the legs vibrate. Sit, soft eyes, long exhales. (Ex. 1)

citation: Alexander Lowen, The Way to Vibrant Health
name: Belly, hips, wiggle, settle
summary: Seven and a quarter minutes below the diaphragm: let the belly all the way out, circle the hips, wiggle your ass with no correct form at all, then lie down and rock the pelvis with the breath. Reach for it when the morning is tight, controlled and slightly wired in the lower back, when the breath sits high in the chest and won't drop, or when the check-in has the flavor of should and rules rather than want — the pointless wiggle is the cheapest exit from that. Take it up when it appeals and skip it when it doesn't; the moment it becomes a daily requirement it stops working.

steps.title: 1. Belly out
steps.text: Stand with your feet about eight inches apart, knees slightly bent, weight forward without lifting the heels. Let the lower belly out as far as it will go and breathe there. Notice whether it stays out or quietly gets sucked back in the moment your attention moves. (Ex. 3)

steps.title: 2. Hips in circles
steps.text: Feet a foot apart, knees bent halfway, hands on hips. Press down through the left foot and let the pelvis swing left, roll it forward onto both feet, press the right foot and swing right, then draw it back. Keep the upper body still and the belly soft. Several circles each way. (Ex. 35)

steps.title: 3. Duck wiggle
steps.text: Bend both knees fully with your feet flat, weight toward the front of the feet, lean forward and cock your ass backward. Now move it side to side by itself, without swaying your legs or turning your trunk. There is no correct form here and that is the entire point. (Ex. 38)

steps.title: 4. Rock and breathe
steps.text: Lie down, knees bent, feet flat, hands on the belly. Rock the pelvis slightly back as you breathe in with the belly out, and forward as you breathe out. Slow breaths, sound on the exhale. Tingling in the hands only means you are overbreathing — ease off and it fades. (Ex. 5-A)

steps.title: 5. Fold and settle
steps.text: Stand and hang forward, knees slightly bent, and let the legs shake. Then sit, soften your eyes, and take a few long exhales. (Ex. 1)

citation: Alexander Lowen, The Way to Vibrant Health
name: Stand, fall, fold, rest
summary: Seven and a half minutes of legs, ending face-down on the floor: stand on one leg until it shakes, then kneel and deliberately let a knee collapse under you, then fold, then rest in the knee-chest position. Reach for it on a wired, anxious, already-buzzing morning — restless, mind going, too much energy rather than too little — where the job is to put charge into the ground rather than raise more. Not the one for a flat morning, and not one to run every day; it works best picked up when the state actually calls for it.

steps.title: 1. Let down
steps.text: Stand with your feet parallel about eight inches apart, knees soft, weight forward on the balls of the feet, belly out, pelvis loose and tipped back, pelvic floor dropped. Four or five audible breaths. You are looking for how far you can let down into your feet, not for more energy. (Ex. 13)

steps.title: 2. One leg
steps.text: Bend the left knee and shift all your weight onto the left foot, the right foot resting flat on the floor. Breathe and hold until it gets uncomfortable, then change. Twice on each leg. Once the leg starts to vibrate most of the ache goes with it. (Ex. 19)

steps.title: 3. Fall
steps.text: Kneel on a rug. Put the left foot flat about six inches in front of the right knee, fingertips on the floor well ahead of it, and shift your weight forward onto your hands so the right foot lifts off. Hold until it is too much, then let the left knee simply collapse onto the floor. Twice each side. The falling is the exercise, not the holding. (Ex. 26)

steps.title: 4. Fold
steps.text: Stand and hang forward, knees slightly bent, fingertips toward the floor with no weight on them. Slowly bend and straighten the knees a few times, never locking, until the legs tremble — then hold and let the shaking have you. (Ex. 1)

steps.title: 5. Rest
steps.text: Kneel and stretch forward, hands flat in front of you, elbows spread, forehead resting on your hands, back arched so the belly hangs loose. Breathe into the low belly. Then sit up, soft eyes, and go straight into the sit. (Ex. 21)

citation: Alexander Lowen, The Way to Vibrant Health
name: Head, eyes, hands, breath
summary: Five minutes flat, almost no exertion: one fold, then roll the head and move the eyes, then charge the hands until they tingle, then sit and breathe into the belly. Reach for it on a scattered, in-the-head, already-planning morning where the problem is attention rather than energy, and also when he is simply short on time — it is the shortest warm-up in the library and needs no bolster and barely any floor. It is a sensing practice with no target and no release, which is exactly why it is worth skipping whenever it feels like a box to tick.

steps.title: 1. Fold
steps.text: Hang forward, knees slightly bent, fingertips toward the floor, head heavy. Breathe through an open mouth and let the legs do whatever they do. Just enough to get out of your head and into your feet. (Ex. 1)

steps.title: 2. Head and eyes
steps.text: Let the head fall forward and roll it slowly in a circle three times each way, shoulders hanging low, blinking as things pass your eyes. Then hold the head still and look right, blink, glance up and down, then the same to the left; then roll the eyes slowly in circles both ways. Glance, never stare. (Ex. 50, 61)

steps.title: 3. Charge the hands
steps.text: Sit cross-legged. Put your fingertips together, spread the fingers and press them against each other with the palms held apart, turn the hands in toward your chest and push them out as far as they will go. Breathe easily for a full minute, then let the hands hang loose and look at your fingertips. Now cup them and bring them slowly to within a couple of inches of each other and feel what is between them. (Ex. 54)

steps.title: 4. Sit and breathe
steps.text: Sit cross-legged leaning slightly forward so you feel your sit bones pressing into the floor, belly out, head loose. Hands on the belly, breathe into it without forcing, eyes soft. (Ex. 51, 63)
